---
title: "Statistical methodology"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Statistical methodology}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

For gene $g$ and sample $i$, version 0.1.0 fits

$$\log(\mu_{gi})=o_i+X_i\beta_g,$$

where $o_i=\log(N_i f_i)$ uses the original library size $N_i$ and TMMwsp
factor $f_i$. The design starts with one named column per batch and adds
nonredundant group/covariate columns. Full rank is required.

Automatic reference scoring fits each batch separately with an explicit
intercept and the estimable local biological terms. Unused factor levels are
dropped. Rank-deficient terms are removed one at a time and recorded; if no
biological term is estimable, the recorded fallback is an intercept-only
model. Thus the baseline biological group never has a mean model with an
all-zero row and no intercept.

For prediction, $X_i^{ref}$ copies $X_i$ and replaces only its batch indicators.
The observed and reference means are

$$\hat\mu_{gi}=\exp(o_i+X_i\hat\beta_g),\qquad
\hat\mu^{ref}_{gi}=\exp(o_i+X_i^{ref}\hat\beta_g).$$

The deterministic mapping uses

$$u=F_{old}(y-1)+\tfrac12P_{old}(Y=y),\qquad y^*=F_{ref}^{-1}(u),$$

with probabilities clamped to finite machine bounds. Both distributions are
negative binomial with variance $\mu+\phi\mu^2$.

edgeR QL diagnostics use

$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_{gi})=\sigma_g^2(\mu_{gi}+\phi_g\mu_{gi}^2).$$

With edgeR 4, the QL fit uses `glmQLFit(..., dispersion = NULL, robust = TRUE,
legacy = FALSE)`, which estimates a global NB dispersion rather than accepting
tagwise dispersions. Baseline tagwise NB dispersion, the global NB dispersion
used by QL, and moderated QL dispersion $\sigma_g^2$ are stored separately. QL
does not supply a CDF, so it is never passed to `pnbinom()` or `qnbinom()`.

Input preparation is separate from model validation. Lossless conversions are
announced and recorded in `diagnostics$input_actions`. Rounding fractional
counts and summing duplicate gene identifiers require explicit opt-in and are
marked as lossy or consequential. Negative, non-finite, normalized, ambiguous,
or otherwise biologically unsafe inputs remain errors. Genes all zero in a
batch are unsupported and returned unchanged with an explicit status.
